questions.question_text: Which expression is the simplified form of $\cot\theta\sec\theta$?

options.why: Inverted the cosecant ratio after cancelling cosine.
Multiplied reciprocal ratios instead of substituting quotient definition.
Cancelled sine instead of cosine in the quotient expansion.
Subtracted from the same trig ratio instead of applying Pythagorean substitution.
Added terms instead of factoring the Pythagorean identity.
Replaced cosine squared with tangent squared.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\tan x - \tan x\sin^{2}x$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$.

options.why: Subtracted incorrectly inside the bracket factor.
Multiplied sine squared instead of cancelling one power of cosine.
Divided by cosine squared instead of multiplying.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan x - \tan x\sin^{2}x$
$= \tan x(1 - \sin^{2}x)$
$= \tan x\cos^{2}x$
$= \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} \times \cos^{2}x$
$= \sin x\cos x$

questions.question_text: Simplify $\dfrac{1}{\sin\phi} - \sin\phi$ into a product of two trigonometric functions.

options.why: Omitted the denominator sine term when combining fractions.
Swapped cotangent for tangent in the final product.
Replaced cosine over sine with cosecant instead of cotangent.
Replaced secant squared minus tangent squared with zero instead of one.
Expanded the binomial product as a sum of squares instead of a difference of squares.
Confused secant squared with cosecant squared in the secondary Pythagorean identity.
Added one fraction instead of summing both simplified unit terms.
Inverted denominators before substituting Pythagorean identities.
Subtracted the two fractions instead of adding them.
Inverted the quotient identity, replacing cosine over sine with tangent.
Added the numerators instead of subtracting them.
Omitted cancelling the common factor of sine between the numerator and denominator.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin x}{1 - \cos x} - \dfrac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x}$
$= \dfrac{\sin x(1 + \cos x) - \sin x(1 - \cos x)}{(1 - \cos x)(1 + \cos x)}$
$= \dfrac{(\sin x + \sin x\cos x) - (\sin x - \sin x\cos x)}{1 - \cos^{2}x}$
$= \dfrac{2\sin x\cos x}{\sin^{2}x}$
$= \dfrac{2\cos x}{\sin x}$
$= 2\cot x$

options.why: Expanded as a sum of squares instead of difference of squares.
Reversed the terms in the Pythagorean identity secant squared minus tangent squared.
Subtracted trigonometric terms to obtain zero instead of applying the Pythagorean identity.
